tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local continuation fixture from the prior multi_agent checkpoint. Worker W1 has stable effect_identity=E and intended payload H1 after acknowledgement_lost_after_possible_commit. The checkpointed authoritative claim observation for E is monotonic generation 12, payload H1, owner W1. A later authoritative lookup returns the same payload H1 at strictly newer generation 13 but owner W2. The fixture tests only whether payload equality permits W1 to attribute its lost-ack operation as the current success, retry create, retry overwrite, or otherwise mutate E after observing the newer generation/owner. No public-source probe, O/downstream or other-worker semantics, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, real simultaneous repository write, richer-mode arbitration, external coordinator, or optional second semantic leaf was used.

reconciliation_result.required_action: preserve generation 13 canonical state; treat W1's historical outcome as non-attributable; require any future W1 action to obtain a fresh atomic claim against the current generation rather than inferring success or replay permission from payload equality

observations: The canonical generation advanced from 12 to 13 while the payload returned to the same value H1, creating an ABA-style equality case in which content equality does not imply identity of the committed claim instance.
The newer canonical record is owned by W2, so W1's checkpointed ownership is stale even though the payload bytes/hash match W1's intended payload.
Suppressing W1 create and overwrite retries prevents a stale worker from converting payload equality into duplicate or conflicting mutation after an intervening claim transition.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, payload equality is insufficient for idempotent success attribution after acknowledgement loss when an authoritative monotonic generation proves an intervening transition and the current owner differs. A generation/owner fence rejects the stale replay without external hosted coordination or richer-mode arbitration. This fixture does not prove that any concrete allowed repository/API transport exposes atomic single-winner claims, monotonic generations, or owner/fencing semantics, and it does not prove liveness under contention.
unresolved_children: Availability of an atomic single-winner claim primitive keyed by stable effect identity on an allowed zero-cost quota-independent transport remains unproven.
A real allowed transport exposing authoritative monotonic generation plus current-owner or equivalent fencing-token identity remains unproven.

Owner-label reuse remains untested: a newer generation may again report owner W1 for a different W1 process/incarnation, so logical owner equality may be unsafe without a per-claim token or worker incarnation epoch.
No liveness claim is made when fresh atomic claim acquisition remains unavailable or indefinitely contended.
